page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 instance family, powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 480 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Additionally, the instance incorporates 2835 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes Intel hardware extensions such as AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Performance benchmarks demonstrate robust capabilities across general and data-intensive tasks. The server delivers a PassMark CPU score of 68,963.55 and multi-core CPU performance of 49,841.59 under stress testing. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 259.05 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression performs at 36.3 GB/sec. Data structure and web hosting benchmarks reveal notable efficiency, yielding 84.18 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 72.52 GB/sec. On CPU-based small LLM workloads, the system achieves 239.1 prompt tokens per second on a 7B model.

By combining dedicated vCPUs with 2.83 TB of fast local NVMe storage and high L3 cache density, the instance offers strong resource density for disk-bound and memory-sensitive services without requiring dedicated memory-optimized SKUs. A key architectural tradeoff is the reliance on simultaneous multithreading across 24 physical cores to supply 48 vCPUs, which may impact workloads highly sensitive to core contention. This instance is well-suited for relational databases, enterprise web serving, Redis caching clusters, ETL pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
